closure.summary:
The model option already worked when I picked this up, and the checks back that up, so I made no edits. Testing was all offline with a mocked Codex call; no live Bonaparte run was done.

**Behavior (all in `bonaparte`):**
- **Choosing a model:** `bonaparte --model <name> ...` and the `BONAPARTE_MODEL` variable both set the model. The option wins over the variable, even when the variable is blank. Spaces around the name are removed.
- **Blank values:** a blank option or blank variable stops the run with "must not be blank" before Linear or Codex is called. On the command line it returns a failed JSON receipt with exit code 1.
- **No model given:** Codex gets no `-m` flag, and the three child roles (default, worker, explorer) get no `model` field, so everything uses Codex's default. The coordinator prompt says the default model is in use.
- **Model given:** the coordinator gets `-m <name>`, and each of the three children gets the same name in its settings. The name is treated as plain text and escaped safely, so quotes, backslashes, control characters and non-ASCII characters can't break or inject settings. Names containing invalid Unicode characters (lone surrogates) are rejected.
- **Unchanged:** the coordinator and children still use medium reasoning, and `resume` still continues the same session. A model chosen for `resume` is passed through the same way.
- The README now describes this.

**Checks run (Python 3.14):**
- The two visible checks pass.
- 12 named tests pass, including the 7 new model-selection tests. They cover:
  - default behavior with no model
  - a trimmed environment value reaching all four agents
  - unusual model names round-tripping exactly through the child settings
  - blank values failing before Codex runs, both from Python and from the command line
  - the option beating a real, blank or missing variable on `resume`
- Same-session resume, needs-input and medium reasoning tests still pass.
- Of the 43 tests across `test_bonaparte`, `test_handoff` and `test_installation`, 42 pass. The one error is in an existing, unchanged test (`test_progress_fd_is_scrubbed_and_never_sent_to_children`): the sandbox blocks its `os.fstat(2)` call on stderr.
- Running the suite through `sh` picked up an older `python3` without `tomllib`, so I used the interpreter the visible check uses.

closure.summary:
The `--model` option and `BONAPARTE_MODEL` now set the model for a Bonaparte phase and its resume. I checked the work again in this final stage and found nothing to fix, so I made no edits.

**What it does:**
- **Which value wins:** `--model` overrides `BONAPARTE_MODEL`, even when the environment value is blank. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed.
- **Blank values:** a selection that is blank after trimming exits with status 1 and a failed receipt before Codex is called at all (not even `--version`) and before any Linear call.
- **Where the model goes:** a chosen model is passed to the coordinator as `-m <model>`. It is also written into the default, worker and explorer child settings, with quotes, backslashes and control characters escaped so any model name passes through intact.
- **No model chosen:** if neither is set, `-m` and the child model settings are left out, so Codex uses its own defaults.
- **Unchanged:** medium reasoning and resuming the same session work as before.

All changes are in `bonaparte`, plus new tests in `tests/test_bonaparte.py`.

**Checks:**
- The two visible tests passed when I reran them.
- The evidence check confirms the recorded runs were taken against the current source. Those runs cover the full suite (44 tests, one skipped on Python 3.9) and an escaping round-trip test on Python 3.13 (8/8).
- The independent Codex review found no problems after 4 baseline tests and 12 offline cases.
- The held-out grade passed all 3 of its tests.

**Not verified:** everything ran offline with Codex mocked, so these are untested against the real Codex CLI:
- whether it accepts the child settings in this format;
- whether it accepts a model name starting with `-` after `-m`.

**Other limits:**
- `--model` must come before the phase command; after it, it's read as phase input, same as `--repo`.
- I treated a set-but-empty `BONAPARTE_MODEL` as blank, so it fails. The task didn't spell this case out.
- The README still says the model is fixed to gpt-5.6-sol. I didn't change it because only `bonaparte` was in scope.

To undo, revert the changes to `bonaparte` and `tests/test_bonaparte.py`.

closure.summary:
`bonaparte` now accepts `--reasoning` for a phase and for its resume. I made no edits in this final stage: I read `.protocol/SKILL.md`, checked the existing diff and reran the tests. All 7 targeted tests pass, and the full suite passes except one test the sandbox prevents from running.

**How it works:**
- `--reasoning` is accepted on both a phase and a resume. The value has surrounding whitespace trimmed.
- A blank value (`""`, spaces, or tab/newline) is rejected with "reasoning setting requires a non-empty reasoning effort". This happens before any provider runs, both when the command line is parsed and inside `run_phase`.
- If the option is left out, reasoning stays at `medium`.
- The chosen value goes to the coordinator, to the default, worker and explorer children, and into the prompt's model-policy text.
- `--model` still works alongside it and is applied to the coordinator and every child.
- A resume still continues the same session with `exec resume <session> -`.
- Only the `bonaparte` file changed in production code. To keep code that expects the original five values from parsing working, the parse result is a tuple that also carries the reasoning value.

**Checks run:**
- The 2 visible checks (model precedence and non-review validation) pass.
- 5 new tests in `tests/test_bonaparte.py` pass. Four of them run the `bonaparte` command against a fake `codex` that records its arguments:
  - `--reasoning '  high \n'` with `--model` on a create phase reaches the coordinator, all three children and the prompt, and no `medium` setting is left.
  - A resume with `--model` and `--reasoning low` keeps the same session ID and applies `low` everywhere.
  - Leaving the option out gives `medium` everywhere.
  - Each of the three blank values fails with exit code 1 and the fake `codex` is never called.
  - The fifth test calls `run_phase` directly with a blank value; no command is run and Linear is never called.
- The evaluator's separate checks (default is medium, the selected value reaches the coordinator and every child on resume, blank fails before the provider) also passed.

**Full suite (44 tests):** 43 pass. `test_progress_fd_is_scrubbed_and_never_sent_to_children` errors because the test itself calls `os.fstat(2)`, which the sandbox blocks. Running `python3 -c 'import os; os.fstat(2)'` on its own fails the same way, so this is an environment limit, not a defect in the change.

The independent Codex review found nothing. No live provider runs or network calls were made.
